title: Structural isomerism; Stereoisomerism (E/Z and optical)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR04#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR04#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR04#t4 term and clue written for the game; OR04#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR04#N.4, OR05#N.4a, OR04#N.7, OR05#N.5, OR04#N.8, OR05#N.8, OR04#N.9, OR05#N.12, OR05#N.14c.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Position isomers
items.clue: The same group at a different place, e.g. propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol.

items.label: Functional group isomers
items.clue: One molecular formula but different families, e.g. propanal and propanone.

items.label: Tertiary alcohol
items.clue: The carbon carrying the –OH is bonded to three other carbons, as in (CH₃)₃COH.

items.label: Chain isomers
items.clue: One molecular formula but different carbon skeletons, e.g. hexane and 2-methylpentane.

questions.stem: Which pair of compounds are position isomers?
questions.explanation: Both are C₅H₁₂O alcohols on the same unbranched chain; only the –OH position differs (pentan-1-ol, pentan-3-ol).

questions.stem: In one stereoisomer of 2-chlorobut-2-ene, CH₃CCl=CHCH₃, the Cl atom and the H atom are on the same side of the C=C. Which is correct?

options.text: It is Z, because the Cl atom and the H atom are on the same side.
It is E, because the priority groups, Cl and CH₃, are on opposite sides.
It is Z, because the two CH₃ groups are on the same side.
It has no E/Z isomers, because one of its C=C carbons carries a CH₃ group.

questions.explanation: C2: Cl outranks CH₃. C3: CH₃ outranks H. Cl is on the H side, so it is opposite the CH₃ on C3: E.

questions.stem: Which compound is a tertiary alcohol?
questions.explanation: The carbon carrying –OH is bonded to three carbons (two CH₃, one CH₂CH₃): 2-methylbutan-2-ol is tertiary.

questions.stem: Which compound can exist as E and Z stereoisomers about its C=C bond?
questions.explanation: Each C=C carbon carries an H and a C₂H₅. Rotation is blocked, so the two arrangements are different compounds.

questions.stem: Classify each halogenoalkane. P: (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl. Q: CH₃CHICH₃. R: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane (Br and CH₃ on the same ring carbon). Which row is correct for P, Q and R?
questions.explanation: P: the CH₂Cl carbon is bonded to one carbon. Q: the CHI carbon to two. R: the C–Br carbon to two ring carbons and the CH₃: three.

questions.stem: Which carbon atom in 3-methylhexane, CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH₃, is a chiral centre?

options.text: None, as every group on C3 starts with a carbon atom.

questions.explanation: C3 carries H, CH₃, C₂H₅ and CH₂CH₂CH₃: four different groups.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers, hexane included, have the molecular formula C₆H₁₄?
questions.explanation: Hexane; 2-methylpentane; 3-methylpentane; 2,2-dimethylbutane; 2,3-dimethylbutane. Every other drawing is one of these.

questions.stem: 2-Hydroxypropanoic acid made in the laboratory from non-chiral starting materials is a racemic mixture. Which statement about this sample is correct?

options.text: Its molecules are achiral, which is why it does not rotate plane-polarised light.
It holds equal amounts of both enantiomers, whose rotations cancel.
It contains equal amounts of the E and Z isomers.
Fractional distillation separates it into its two enantiomers.

questions.explanation: Each enantiomer rotates the plane by the same angle in opposite directions. In a 1 : 1 mixture the effects cancel.

questions.stem: Butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, exists as two stereoisomers with identical boiling points. Which explains why there are two?

options.text: Rotation about the C2–C3 bond is restricted, so the molecule has E and Z isomers.
C2 has four different groups, so the molecule cannot be superimposed on its mirror image.
The –OH group can be on C1 or on C2 of the chain, so there are two position isomers of it.
Every molecule has a mirror image, so every organic compound exists as two stereoisomers.

questions.explanation: C2 carries H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅: a chiral centre. The two stereoisomers are enantiomers.
